sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: traffic lights, pedestrian and lane signals, ramp meters, pavement markings, special lanes and traffic officers
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The light, arrow, X and line patterns on these pages are taught with pictures; the dossier uses only the printed captions and text, and the recognition skill is declared as needing an image-based surface [A03].
The left turn on red rule here says traffic must be permitted to travel only in the direction you are turning, while the traffic laws chapter words the same condition without the word only; the dossier records this page's wording [A01].
The road layout captions describe drawings of two-lane, four-lane, divided and three-lane roads; facts from them repeat only what the captions say about passing and turning [A04] [A05].
The pedestrian signal rules are written for pedestrians; they are kept because drivers must anticipate pedestrian movements at signals.
No figure on these pages comes from outside the manual.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
